rounds.text: Tilak Ventures Ltd is heavily under-appreciated because its extraordinary fundamental growth stands in stark contrast to a depressed share price [E53]. Over multiple timeframes, the business has demonstrated exceptional expansion, including a 5-year compounded profit growth of 48% and a 5-year compounded sales growth of 45% [E15, E19]. This momentum has only accelerated in the trailing twelve months, where sales grew 17% and profit surged by 53% [E17, E21], culminating in a quarterly operating margin of 49% in March 2026 compared to 19% in the year-ago quarter [E30]. This operational strength is completely detached from the market valuation. The stock trades at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.65x on a book value of ₹ 1.73 and a P/E ratio of 15.6, well below sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at ₹ 3 per share against a market price of ₹ 1.12, offering a substantial 61.7% margin of safety, while a reverse DCF implies that the current price only demands a modest 4.8% earnings growth [E42, E43, E44]. Balance sheet risk has also been entirely eliminated, with borrowings reduced from ₹ 8.00 Cr to zero, leaving the company debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E37, E38, E57]. Demonstrating ultimate confidence in this disconnect, promoters have increased their stake from 55.62% to 61.98% [E40]. Conceded: [E24, E33, E34, E35, E48, E49, E64]
